notes: Consent URL the CLI prints for the code_exchange scenario (not a request): `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=golden-google-client-id&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A8765&response_type=code&scope=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fcalendar.events&access_type=offline&prompt=consent&state=golden-token-urlsafe-16&code_challenge=0rnfdO8zLHbPYynUP5e9BxvYBwHL12yVVJTRDlfzAis&code_challenge_method=S256`.

`secrets.token_urlsafe` is pinned to `golden-token-urlsafe-<n>` (verifier `golden-token-urlsafe-64`, state `golden-token-urlsafe-16`) and the loopback port to 8765, so the code exchange is reproducible.
The Calendar client uses googleapiclient's bundled discovery document (`cache_discovery=False`, static discovery): no discovery request is sent.

scenarios.description: google_auth.authorize (`atrium calendar google-auth --port 8765`): after the loopback redirect, the authorization_code grant with the PKCE verifier and the loopback redirect_uri.
scenarios.name: code_exchange

scenarios.description: calendar.create_event on Google, timed (location and notes) and all-day: each call builds a fresh service, so google-auth first sends the refresh_token grant, then events.insert with the client-chosen id and sendUpdates=none.
scenarios.name: event_create

scenarios.description: calendar.delete_event on Google (undo): refresh grant, then events.delete with sendUpdates=none.
scenarios.name: event_delete

scenarios.description: An insert answered 409 (id already inserted) and deletes answered 404 and 410 are treated as done.
scenarios.name: already_applied

scenarios.description: calendar.list_events for Google: refresh grant, then events.list (singleEvents, orderBy startTime, maxResults 250) following nextPageToken.
scenarios.name: events_list
